q: A non-renewable resource is a natural substance that is not replenished with the speed at which it is _____.
e: A non-renewable resource is a natural substance that is not replenished with the speed at which it is consumed.

q: Renewable energy sources are also called _____ energy sources.
e: Renewable energy sources (also called non-conventional energy sources) are continuously replenished by natural processes.

q: Non-renewable energy resources include coal, natural gas, crude oil, and _____.
e: Non-renewable energy resources include coal, natural gas, crude oil, and nuclear energy.

q: Renewable resources are replenished naturally and over short periods of time, so are in a virtually _____ supply.
e: Renewable resources are replenished naturally and over short periods of time, so are in a virtually unlimited supply.

q: They cannot be exhausted easily and can be generated at a constant rate for their use _____.
e: They cannot be exhausted easily and can be generated at a constant rate for their use over and over again.

q: In our daily life we use different forms of energy. The most common forms of energy are heat, light and _____.
e: The most common forms of energy are heat, light and electricity.

q: Non-renewable resources occur in limited and exhaustible quantities and cannot be regenerated in a _____ period of time.
e: They occur in limited and exhaustible quantities and cannot be regenerated in a short period of time.

q: Renewable energy sources are continuously replenished by _____ processes.
e: Renewable energy sources are continuously replenished by natural processes.

q: Which of the following is an example of a renewable energy source?
e: Examples of renewable resources include solar energy, hydro energy, wind energy and geothermal energy.
